# wa-format — full API digest

> Bidirectional WhatsApp formatting library. `toHTML`: WhatsApp markup to safe
> HTML. `toWA`: supported HTML back to WhatsApp markup. Core is dependency-free;
> the bundled MCP server uses the Model Context Protocol SDK. Works in Node ≥20
> and modern browsers. Ships ESM, CJS and TypeScript declarations.

- Site: https://whatsapp-html.os.darcas.app/
- Repo: https://github.com/DarCas/wa-format
- Package: @darcas/wa-format v0.5.0, MIT

## Install

npm: `npm i @darcas/wa-format` · pnpm: `pnpm add @darcas/wa-format` ·
yarn: `yarn add @darcas/wa-format` · bun: `bun add @darcas/wa-format`

## toHTML(input, options?)

`toHTML(input: string, options?: FormatOptions): string`

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `style` | `"semantic" \| "legacy"` | `"semantic"` | `semantic` emits `<b>`/`<i>`/`<s>`; `legacy` emits `<strong>`/`<em>`/`<s>`. |
| `lineBreaks` | `boolean` | `true` | Render `\n` as `<br>`. When `false`, newlines stay `\n`. |
| `trim` | `boolean` | `true` | Trim leading/trailing whitespace before parsing. |

Empty or whitespace-only input returns `""`. Non-string input throws `TypeError`.

```ts
toHTML("*Bold*, _italic_, ~strike~ and `code`.")
```

## toWA(html, options?)

`toWA(html: string, options?: ToWAOptions): string`

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bullet` | `"-" \| "*"` | `"-"` | Marker used for bulleted lists. |

Tag mapping: `<b>`/`<strong>` → `*`, `<i>`/`<em>` → `_`, `<s>`/`<strike>`/`<del>`
→ `~`, `<code>` → backticks, `<pre>` → fenced block, `<blockquote>` → `> `,
`<ul>`/`<li>` → `- `, `<ol>`/`<li>` → `N. ` (with `start`), `<a href>` →
`text (url)`, `<br>` → break, `<p>`/`<div>`/`<h1>`–`<h6>` → line containers.
Unknown tags are unwrapped; entities are decoded.

```ts
toWA("<b>Hello</b> <i>world</i>")        // "*Hello* _world_"
toWA("<blockquote>a<br>b</blockquote>")  // "> a\n> b"
toWA("<ul><li>one</li><li>two</li></ul>") // "- one\n- two"
```

## parse / renderHtml / parseHtml

- `parse(input: string): Document` — WhatsApp text to AST. Line endings
  normalized before parsing.
- `renderHtml(document: Document, options: ResolvedOptions): string` — AST to
  HTML with resolved options.
- `parseHtml(html: string): HtmlNode[]` — low-level HTML fragment parser used
  by `toWA`.
- Also exported: `resolveOptions`, `DEFAULT_OPTIONS`, `FormatOptions`,
  `ResolvedOptions`, `ToWAOptions`, AST node types.

```ts
import {parse, renderHtml, resolveOptions} from "@darcas/wa-format"
const html = renderHtml(parse("*Hello*"), resolveOptions())
```

## Behavior rules

- Markers must touch content: `*bold*` is bold, `* bold *` is literal.
- A marker inside a word (`snake_case`, `2*3*4`) stays literal.
- No escape character: wrap markers in code to show them literally.
- Code is opaque: markers inside `` `code` `` or fenced blocks never parse.
- Lists need a space: `- text`, `* text`, `1. text`. Up to two digits for
  numbered lists. No nested lists.
- Consecutive quote lines group into one `<blockquote>` with `<br>` between.
- All text is HTML-escaped (`&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, `'`); output is safe to inject.
- `\n` between text lines becomes `<br>`; newlines around block elements are
  absorbed by the element.
- `toWA` is lossy: literal markers, markers adjacent to word characters, and
  backticks inside code cannot round-trip. Guarantee: HTML idempotence,
  `toHTML(toWA(html)) === toHTML(html)`.

## MCP server

`wa-format-mcp` over stdio (Node ≥20).

```json
{
    "mcpServers": {
        "wa-format": {
            "command": "npx",
            "args": ["-y", "-p", "@darcas/wa-format", "wa-format-mcp"]
        }
    }
}
```

| Tool | Arguments | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `whatsapp_to_html` | `text` (required), `style`, `lineBreaks`, `trim` | HTML |
| `html_to_whatsapp` | `html` (required), `bullet` | WhatsApp text |

Both tools: read-only, non-destructive, idempotent, closed-world — safe to
auto-approve.

## Facts

0 core dependencies · ESM + CJS + types · 80 tests · Node ≥20 · MIT.
